claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about your son Alex.

To help me assess his eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old - he was born in February 2017.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in February 2017, making him 8 years old.

**Are you the parent or guardian of Alex, and do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and I have parental responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he lives with me, but we don't actually live in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's important information.

**Which country do you and Alex currently live in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're currently living abroad - we moved overseas a while ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's relevant to the eligibility assessment.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, what is your current immigration status in the country where you're living?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, yes. We're just living abroad temporarily at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you currently working or paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or have you done so recently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working in the UK or paying National Insurance there at the moment - we've been living abroad for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's useful to know.

**Are you working in the country where you're currently living, and if so, are you paying social security contributions there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am working here and paying into the local social security system.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**Is Alex currently attending school or receiving education in the country where you're living, or is he registered with a school in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's going to school here where we live - he's enrolled in the local school system.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

**One more question to clarify your situation: Do you intend to return to the UK permanently, or are you planning to stay abroad long-term? And has there been any break in your residence in the UK before you moved abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're not sure exactly how long we'll be abroad - it could be a few more years at least. We've been living outside the UK for a while now, so there's been quite a gap since we last lived there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider the rules based on your circumstances:

You are a British citizen living abroad with your son Alex (age 8, born February 2017). You're currently working and paying social security contributions in your country of residence, and Alex is attending school there. You're not currently working or paying National Insurance in the UK, and you've been living abroad for an extended period with no recent UK residence.

Based on the UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, Child Benefit is primarily available to those who are:
- Responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 if in full-time education)
- Residing in the UK
- Meeting certain residency and work/National Insurance contribution requirements

Since you and Alex are currently living abroad and have been for an extended period, and you're not paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, this affects your eligibility. While being a British citizen is relevant, the key requirement is that you must be living in the UK to claim Child Benefit, or meet specific exemptions related to UK work or contributions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Outcome: You are not currently eligible for Child Benefit.**

Here's why:

While Alex meets the age requirement for Child Benefit (he's 8 years old), there is a key residency requirement that is not met in your situation. Child Benefit is generally only available to those living in the UK. Since you and Alex are currently living abroad and you have not been paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, you do not qualify under the standard eligibility criteria.

**What you could do:**
- If you and Alex return to the UK and establish residency there, you would then be able to claim Child Benefit, provided you meet the other requirements at that time.
- Your circumstances may change in the future, so it would be worth revisiting your eligibility if your situation changes.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, please feel free to reach out.
